subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and should it be modeled as `tools.selfDeny`, `delegateOnly`, or folded into the per-spawn tool policy work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this changes a security boundary and public config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent semantics or naming.

options.title: Approve explicit delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent self-deny/delegate-only policy that hides tools from the requester's model surface while preserving normal deny-wins semantics for inherited child policy.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy only
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/15032 and its candidate PR own child narrowing, while documenting that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate agent profiles or instructions.

options.title: Reject parent-deny delegation
options.body: Keep the monotonic policy model unchanged and close this design after documenting the security rationale and separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent self-deny/delegate-only policy that hides tools from the requester's model surface while preserving normal deny-wins semantics for inherited child policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about public config and security-boundary semantics, and Peter is the strongest prior review/routing signal in the related issue history.
